supporting_article_titles: Pack Spec Drives Inventory: Nestlé's Supply Chain Strategy
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: Packaging/SKU complexity can be quantified as inventory positions and working-capital risk before product specifications are locked, enabling a repeatable pre-launch decision workflow.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: new product/pack design → SKU/pack configuration → sourcing constraints → inventory positions → P&L approval
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: quantify the inventory and working-capital penalty of pack/SKU choices before launch
raw_opportunities.current_friction: Brand and packaging choices create combinatorial inventory positions, single-source dependencies and later repacking/firefighting; the cost is often discovered after specs are fixed.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: web calculator/decision ledger that converts flavor × pack count × distribution-node choices, MOQ, shelf life and sourcing constraints into inventory positions, working-capital-at-risk and simpler alternatives
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A pre-launch Pack Complexity Cost Desk that shows brand teams the dollar cost of each packaging/SKU choice before it is approved.
raw_opportunities.why_now: Nestlé described a concrete 3×4×3 example producing 36 inventory positions and advocated translating complexity into dollars before design lock.

evidence_notes.source_fact: Packaging World article fully read; Nestlé example and workflow are explicit.
evidence_notes.trakya_transferability_hypothesis: Food and packaged-goods plants in the Trakya industrial corridor plausibly face pack-count, MOQ and packaging-spec complexity; local existence should be verified before Lüleburgaz scope.

supporting_article_titles: New ANSI Standard Completes Industrial Mobile Robot Safety Series
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: ANSI/A3 R15.08-3-2026 adds explicit user-side lifecycle duties for daily IMR operation, including risk assessment, management of change, training, reviews and inspections.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: IMR deployment → daily operation → change management → training → periodic inspection/review → evidence retention
raw_opportunities.target_customer: factories and warehouses operating industrial mobile robots
raw_opportunities.buyer: EHS manager, automation manager or plant manager
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: maintain auditable day-to-day IMR safety obligations after commissioning
raw_opportunities.current_friction: Robot safety evidence is often split across risk assessments, training records, change logs and inspection sheets, while the new standard emphasizes continued-use responsibilities.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: IMR safety lifecycle register with robot/application inventory, change-control workflow, training matrix, inspection schedule, risk-review reminders and evidence export
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A lightweight IMR Safety Ops desk that turns continued-use robot safety duties into recurring evidence workflows.
raw_opportunities.why_now: Part 3 was announced as completing the R15.08 series and specifically addresses user responsibilities during continued operation.

evidence_notes.source_fact: Automation World article fully read; requirements listed explicitly.
evidence_notes.trakya_transferability_hypothesis: Automotive suppliers, warehouses and manufacturers in Trakya adopting AMR/IMR systems could pilot the workflow; local installed-base evidence requires validation.

supporting_article_titles: How Pearl Crop Turned to Rented Robots to Combat Seasonal Labor Concerns
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: Robot rental/try-before-buy makes automation economically accessible for short seasonal peaks rather than requiring permanent capex.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: season forecast → temporary labor/throughput gap → automation suitability → rental duration/robot count → deployment → ROI review
raw_opportunities.buyer: plant manager, operations manager or owner
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: decide when renting robots beats seasonal labor or buying automation
raw_opportunities.current_friction: Seasonal peaks create short-lived palletizing/material-handling bottlenecks, but capex automation can be hard to justify and temporary labor is scarce.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: rental-vs-labor-vs-purchase scenario calculator with peak-window demand, shift hours, case weights, throughput, rental term and payback/constraint comparison
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A Seasonal Automation Planner that tells processors how many rental robots they need and whether rental beats labor or purchase.
raw_opportunities.why_now: Pearl Crop reported using six rented robots for a two-month harvest concentration and immediate throughput/safety benefits.

evidence_notes.source_fact: Food Engineering case study fully read.
evidence_notes.trakya_transferability_hypothesis: Food/agri processing and seasonal production workflows are transferable to Trakya; specific Lüleburgaz pilot sectors need fresh local validation.

supporting_article_titles: Cargo thieves are ‘laundering freight’ through the supply chain, Cornell warns
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: Cargo theft increasingly uses document/identity changes across cross-docks and transfers; an auditable chain of changes to commodity descriptions, BOLs and seals can expose laundering patterns.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: load tender → pickup → cross-dock/transfer → BOL/commodity/seal changes → port/export → buyer receipt
raw_opportunities.target_customer: 3PLs, shippers, freight brokers, warehouses and cargo insurers
raw_opportunities.buyer: security/risk manager, logistics director or claims investigator
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: detect suspicious shipment identity changes and preserve an auditable custody trail
raw_opportunities.current_friction: A stolen load can be repeatedly transferred and re-papered until legitimate buyers cannot recognize its origin; each document change breaks visibility.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: shipment identity ledger that fingerprints load attributes and flags changes in BOL, commodity description, carrier/broker, seal, cross-dock and custody events; supports QR/scannable verification and case evidence export
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A Freight Identity Ledger that flags when a shipment’s paperwork and custody mutate in ways consistent with cargo laundering.
raw_opportunities.why_now: FreightWaves reported TAPA expert Scott Cornell describing freight laundering and explicitly pointing to digital bills of lading and auditable description changes as a countermeasure.

evidence_notes.source_fact: FreightWaves article fully read; mechanism and proposed digital trail are explicit.
evidence_notes.trakya_transferability_hypothesis: Trakya's road freight, warehouses and European export corridor make the workflow potentially relevant; local theft/problem evidence must be validated.

supporting_article_titles: USPS, Amazon partner on same-day delivery pilot
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: A second midday injection into an incumbent last-mile network allows orders placed later in the day to qualify for same-day service, creating a capacity/cutoff orchestration problem.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: order cutoff → midday injection → facility sort capacity → route allocation → same-day delivery window
raw_opportunities.target_customer: regional parcel carriers, retailers and 3PLs operating same-day networks
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: model extra same-day injection windows without overloading sort/route capacity
raw_opportunities.current_friction: Adding later cutoffs changes facility volume caps, route requirements and dispatch windows; spreadsheet planning can hide infeasible promises.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: same-day injection scenario planner using cutoff, drop time, facility cap, route count, driver capacity and delivery window to test service promises
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A Same-Day Cutoff Simulator for carriers and retailers adding midday injection waves to existing last-mile networks.
raw_opportunities.why_now: USPS/Amazon pilot adds a 12–1 p.m. injection with explicit facility volume and route caps for 2–8 p.m. delivery.

evidence_notes.source_fact: Supply Chain Dive article fully read.
evidence_notes.trakya_transferability_hypothesis: Transferable to regional delivery/3PL operations but no Lüleburgaz-specific evidence in assigned material.

supporting_article_titles: Mars hikes sustainably sourced cocoa but falls short of 2025 100% goal
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: Responsible-sourcing programs increasingly combine supplier sourcing percentages, land-conversion rules, farmer programs and disease/climate interventions, creating evidence reconciliation beyond a single certification field.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: supplier program → sourced-volume evidence → farm/land criteria → intervention evidence → annual target reconciliation/report
raw_opportunities.target_customer: food brands and ingredient importers with responsible-sourcing commitments
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: reconcile supplier evidence against sourcing targets and explain gaps before annual reporting
raw_opportunities.current_friction: Progress data spans supplier volumes, land-use criteria, farmer programs and interventions; annual target misses are discovered during reporting rather than continuously.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: supplier evidence ledger with target denominator, verified-volume numerator, criteria checklist, gap forecast, intervention log and audit-ready annual evidence pack
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A Responsible Sourcing Gap Ledger that continuously reconciles supplier evidence against public sourcing targets.
raw_opportunities.why_now: Mars reported 98% responsible-sourcing coverage versus a 100% target and described multi-country supplier/farmer interventions.

evidence_notes.source_fact: Supply Chain Dive article fully read.
evidence_notes.trakya_transferability_hypothesis: Transferable to food manufacturers/importers but local scope needs evidence.

supporting_article_titles: OpenAI apes AWS Marketplace while Anthropic remains stubbornly Microsoftian
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: AI model distribution is becoming a multi-provider marketplace problem rather than a single-cloud procurement decision, increasing the need to compare deployment/provider constraints.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: AI use case → model choice → inference provider/marketplace → data/residency/cost constraints → approval → deployment
raw_opportunities.target_customer: SMEs and enterprise AI/platform teams using multiple model/inference providers
raw_opportunities.buyer: AI platform lead, solution architect or procurement lead
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: document and compare model-provider deployment choices without locking evaluation to one marketplace
raw_opportunities.current_friction: The same model ecosystem can be exposed through different inference providers and marketplaces, while teams track price, region, data handling and contractual constraints manually.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: vendor-neutral model deployment decision register with model/provider matrix, residency/contract fields, evaluation evidence and approval trail
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A Model Deployment Decision Desk that separates model choice from inference-provider and marketplace choice.
raw_opportunities.why_now: The Register reported OpenAI expanding a marketplace approach including third-party inference provider Baseten, highlighting provider-neutral distribution.

evidence_notes.source_fact: The Register article verified; opportunity is an inference from distribution fragmentation.

supporting_article_titles: Bayer invests €30 million in its Villefranche-sur-Saône factory
raw_opportunities.novelty_delta: Manufacturing footprint investment decisions increasingly hinge on comparing sites under global cost/competition pressure, creating a structured pre-capex evidence problem.
raw_opportunities.affected_workflow: capacity need → candidate site comparison → labor/energy/logistics/qualification constraints → capex case → investment approval
raw_opportunities.buyer: industrial strategy, operations finance or plant-network manager
raw_opportunities.job_to_be_done: build a repeatable evidence-based comparison for which existing site should receive incremental capex
raw_opportunities.current_friction: Site-investment cases are assembled in bespoke spreadsheets and presentations, making assumptions and non-financial constraints hard to compare or audit across plants.
raw_opportunities.product_mechanism: multi-site capex decision ledger with weighted cost, capacity, labor, energy, logistics, regulatory and strategic criteria plus scenario/sensitivity report
raw_opportunities.one_sentence_concept: A Plant Capex Site Comparator that standardizes the evidence behind which existing factory wins the next investment.
raw_opportunities.why_now: L'Usine Nouvelle reported Bayer choosing its French site over a German unit for a €30m investment amid Chinese competitive pressure.

evidence_notes.source_fact: L'Usine Nouvelle article verified; opportunity is a generalized workflow inference.
evidence_notes.trakya_transferability_hypothesis: Multi-site industrial companies and suppliers in Trakya could use the same capex comparison workflow; local evidence needed before assigning Lüleburgaz.
